cases.situation: served or validated (`2xx`, `4xx` invalid) unlike a random sibling, with neither `Deprecation` nor `Sunset`
cases.how: the lab as built: GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/times/{user}, filled from path_seed, answers 200 unlike a random sibling, with neither Deprecation nor Sunset

cases.situation: the operation's method writes: not sent
cases.how: the lab as built: three deprecated operations write (POST /org/{org}/repos, DELETE and PATCH .../comments/{id}) and are not sent

cases.situation: a path without parameters answers like a random sibling: the operation is gone
cases.how: the run reads a local copy of Forgejo's specification with one added operation without path parameters, GET /api/v1/apiguard-deprecated-probe marked deprecated, that Forgejo does not serve: it answers 404 like its random sibling

cases.situation: a path parameter has no value in `path_seed`
cases.how: the run's target.path_seed is emptied, so the deprecated read's path parameters have no value

cases.situation: an answer of this category on any sub-test that does not judge it: 429: refused for the rate of the requests. It says nothing about the guarantee (one rule for every test)
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) answers 429 itself

cases.situation: an answer of this category on any sub-test that does not judge it: 500, 505-508, 510: the application failed. It says nothing about the guarantee (one rule for every test)
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) answers 500 itself

cases.situation: an answer of this category on any sub-test that does not judge it: 502, 503, 504: the gateway could not reach the backend, or the backend did not answer in time. It says nothing about the guarantee (one rule for every test)
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) answers 503 itself

cases.situation: served unlike a random sibling, with `Deprecation` and no `Sunset`
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) adds 'Deprecation: @1688169599' to Forgejo's answer
a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read as the test fills it (times/user-a) answers 410 itself

cases.situation: `405` or `501`: the method is no longer available on the path
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) answers 405 itself

cases.situation: a redirect, a `404` unlike a random sibling, or an answer of no class
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) answers 302 to https://localhost:8443/ itself

cases.situation: an answer of this category on any sub-test that does not judge it: No HTTP response: timeout, connection refused, TLS error, connection reset. It says nothing about the guarantee (one rule for every test)
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) sleeps 7 s before proxying, and the run's read timeout is 5 s

cases.situation: served unlike a random sibling, with a `Sunset` date in the future
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) adds 'Sunset: Sat, 31 Dec 2099 23:59:59 GMT' to Forgejo's answer

cases.situation: served unlike a random sibling, with a `Sunset` that is not an HTTP-date
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) adds 'Sunset: soon' to Forgejo's answer

cases.situation: served unlike a random sibling, with a `Sunset` date that has passed
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on the deprecated read (times/user-a) adds 'Sunset: Wed, 01 Jan 2020 00:00:00 GMT' to Forgejo's answer

cases.situation: a path with parameters answers like a random object: the operation gone, or the seeded object not found
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on times/<any> (the deprecated read and its random siblings) answers the same fixed 404 itself

cases.situation: the calibration of the operation's siblings is unreliable
cases.how: a temporary Kong route on times/<any> (the deprecated read and its random siblings) answers 404 with a body of one of two shapes, alternating, so the two calibration siblings differ

cases.situation: refused (`401`, `403`) without a credential and with user_a's, or without and no user_a account
